description: Exact cross-architecture implementation inventory. Remove entries as policy moves into common code; do not expand debt to make validation pass.

kernel_arch_boottime_initialize.reason: Reads and initializes the hardware-specific monotonic clock source.

kernel_arch_boottime_monotonic_us.reason: Reads the current architecture timer and converts its counter value.

kernel_arch_boottime_refine.reason: Refines boot time against the architecture-specific timer frequency.

kernel_arch_boottime_source_hz.reason: Reports the frequency of the selected hardware clock source.

kernel_arch_boottime_source_name.reason: Reports the name of the selected hardware clock source.

kernel_arch_boottime_timer_tick.reason: Receives ticks from the architecture-specific timer interrupt.

kernel_arch_boottime_vdso_snapshot.reason: Snapshots the architecture counter state used by the shared vDSO time conversion.

kernel_arch_current_request_reschedule.reason: Marks the native current task or per-CPU target so each architecture schedules after the shared syscall policy completes.

kernel_arch_current_rseq_slice_timer_arm.reason: Programs the native per-CPU high-resolution timer after the shared rseq state machine grants a bounded slice.

kernel_arch_current_rseq_slice_timer_can.reason: Restores the native periodic timer after shared rseq syscall entry or revocation ends a slice grant.

kernel_arch_display_deadline_request.reason: Programs the native APIC or ARM counter alarm for a deadline selected by shared display policy and timer arbitration.

kernel_arch_input_work_request.reason: Wakes the architecture scheduler when shared deferred input work is queued from interrupt or process context.

kernel_arch_network_work_request.reason: Wakes the architecture scheduler when a network interrupt queues protocol processing outside hard interrupt context.

kernel_arch_scheduler_cpu_stats.reason: Snapshots counters owned by each architecture scheduler while common code defines their Linux-visible format.

kernel_arch_scheduler_online_cpu_mask.reason: Reports CPUs discovered and brought online by architecture startup code.

kernel_arch_serial_console_device.reason: Maps platform UART hardware to its Linux-visible serial device identity.

kernel_arch_signal_user_stack_pointer.reason: Reads the user stack pointer from the architecture-specific saved register frame.

kernel_arch_signal_wait_block.reason: Parks either a saved user frame or the live syscall stack as required by the entry mechanism.

kernel_arch_vfs_read_resident.reason: Copies a resident prefix from native file-page backing storage with architecture cache pins, backing generations and physical-alias maintenance. Immutable-file eligibility and EOF policy remain in the common VFS reader.

kernel_arch_wait_deadline_request.reason: Programs the native per-CPU APIC or ARM counter using shared finite-wait deadline validation and timer arbitration.

kernel_drm_waiter_cancelled.reason: Resumes the native descriptor wait after shared DRM final-close cancellation: x86 resumes a blocked syscall stack, while ARM re-evaluates and completes a saved poll/select/epoll frame. Client lifetime and cancellation selection remain in common DRM code.

kernel_drm_waiter_ready.reason: Maps a shared DRM waiter notification to native task wake mechanics: x86 resumes a blocked descriptor syscall, while ARM re-evaluates and completes its saved wait frame. Shared DRM code owns event enqueue, waiter identity, registration and readiness ordering.

kernel_drm_waiter_wake_batch_complete.reason: Completes architecture-specific scheduling after a shared DRM waiter callback batch: x86 wakeups already enter its runqueue directly, while ARM selects one runnable target after all saved wait frames have been completed.

kernel_edge_kvm_descriptor_runtime_initi.reason: Connects common KVM objects to each architecture's native process descriptor table and file lifetime rules.

kernel_ptrace_current_syscall.reason: Decodes syscall arguments and results from the architecture-specific saved register frame.

kernel_ptrace_get_regset.reason: Exports architecture-specific Linux general-purpose, floating-point, and extension register sets.

kernel_ptrace_get_thread_area.reason: Exports an architecture-specific Linux thread-local descriptor where the architecture provides that facility.

kernel_ptrace_read_user_area.reason: Reads the architecture-specific Linux ptrace user-register layout at a byte offset.

kernel_ptrace_set_regset.reason: Imports architecture-specific Linux general-purpose, floating-point, and extension register sets.

kernel_ptrace_set_thread_area.reason: Imports an architecture-specific Linux thread-local descriptor where the architecture provides that facility.

kernel_ptrace_write_user_area.reason: Updates the architecture-specific Linux ptrace user-register layout at a byte offset.

kernel_sysv_shm_arch_current_address_spa.reason: Returns the native address-space handle used by architecture VM operations.

kernel_sysv_shm_arch_map.reason: Maps validated shared-memory pages using architecture page-table mechanics.

kernel_sysv_shm_arch_page_allocate.reason: Allocates a native page handle through the architecture VM allocator.

kernel_sysv_shm_arch_page_release.reason: Releases a native page handle through the architecture VM allocator.

kernel_sysv_shm_arch_unmap.reason: Unmaps shared memory using architecture page-table mechanics.

kernel_wait_deadline_poll.reason: Traverses native blocked-task representations and wakes expired shared-policy waits under the x86 owner runqueue lock or ARM serialized runtime lock.

duplicate_policy_migration_target: Move every listed service to one architecture-neutral implementation and retain only the smallest required architecture operation callback.
